articles.title: Eye on Everything
articles.summary: The article reports on an engaging talk by Craig Wandke about the Moon, covering its formation, missions, and observing. It also announces several key upcoming events, including the 16th Annual Bay Area Astronomical Auction and Swap Meet, the AANC's annual star-b-q, and SJAA's star party nights at Yosemite. Additionally, it highlights new coffee service at club meetings and invites member participation for the June 1 meeting.

articles.title: Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This document presents an activities calendar for May and June, detailing various astronomical events such as star parties at multiple state parks, general club meetings, and an observational astronomy class. It also includes information on a swap meet and auction, board meetings, and contact details for news and information.

articles.title: Review: Herald-Bobroff AstroAtlas
articles.summary: This article is a personal review of the Herald-Bobroff AstroAtlas, written by an amateur astronomer. The author, previously a happy owner of the Tirion Sky Atlas 2000.0, recounts his search for a more comprehensive sky chart after repeatedly discovering objects not plotted in his existing atlas. He details a serendipitous encounter at an observing session where he was introduced to the Herald-Bobroff AstroAtlas, which successfully plotted a dim galaxy he had found.

articles.title: Atlas, continued from page 1
articles.summary: This article reviews the AstroAtlas, a comprehensive and physically substantial star atlas noted for its intricate symbology and spiral-bound, double-sided charts. It details six distinct chart series (A through F), progressively increasing in scale and limiting magnitudes for stars and deep-sky objects, covering the entire sky, dense galactic regions, and southern celestial areas. The atlas is praised for its detailed object representations and utility for advanced observers.

articles.title: Overall Impressions
articles.summary: The author shares their initial impressions of using the AstroAtlas, focusing on familiarization with its features. They found the C and D series charts particularly useful and appreciated the detailed object symbols, which helped confirm a faint galaxy observation, though some symbols and labels were occasionally difficult to read.

articles.title: Atlas, continued from page 2
articles.summary: This article reviews the AstroAtlas, praising its depth for deep-sky objects and useful symbols for observing, particularly noting its advantage over Uranometria in object count for more challenging targets. While acknowledging some minor annoyances like unlabeled galaxies, the author finds it a valuable field resource and planning guide for serious observers. The review also compares it to other atlases and provides purchasing information.

articles.title: Comet Blasts Through Tree by Bill O'Shaughnessy
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) hosted a deep sky observing session at Henry Coe State Park on March 16, 1996. Despite initial mediocre skies, conditions improved significantly, and attendees were thrilled by an earlier-than-expected sighting of Comet Hyakutake. The night was considered one of the best ever at Henry Coe due to the excellent skies, mild weather, and the prominent comet.

articles.title: GALILEO MISSION STATUS April 1, 1996
articles.summary: The Galileo spacecraft has resumed playback of atmospheric probe data and made another unsuccessful attempt to free its stuck high-gain antenna. The mission team is actively managing an unexpected tank pressure issue in the helium pressurization system of the propulsion system, which is currently stable. Engineers are also developing a new spacecraft operating system scheduled for upload in May and June, while Galileo continues nominal science operations as it approaches Jupiter.

articles.title: Eye, continued from page 1
articles.summary: This article snippet details an upcoming astronomers' campsite event, providing contact information for sign-up with Jim Van Nuland. It also announces that Bob Brauer, Bob Madden, and an unnamed individual have revised the club's bylaws, which will be available at the June general meeting and online, with a vote scheduled for the July (June 29) general meeting.

articles.title: They Make the Best of Company
articles.summary: The author vividly recounts a nocturnal expedition to dark backcountry roads in March 1996 to observe Comet Hyakutake, likening the magnificent dark-sky view of the comet to an ancient "Star Dragon." The article contrasts this awe-inspiring experience with the disappointing views from light-polluted areas, emphasizing the determination, patience, and persistence required to truly appreciate such rare celestial events. It draws parallels between these efforts and themes of faith and perseverance found in the Book of Job, suggesting that overcoming challenges is essential for a profound astronomical experience.

articles.title: Turned Down Edge
articles.summary: This article clarifies the common mirror-making problem known as "Turned Down Edge" (TDE), arguing that it's often misunderstood as it can result from either excessive wear at the mirror's edge or a central "hole" due to wear in the middle. The author emphasizes that diagnosing the correct root cause is crucial, as applying the wrong correction based on a misdiagnosis can worsen the defect. Furthermore, the article suggests considering the effect of grinding strokes on the tool or lap, rather than solely on the mirror, for a clearer understanding and more effective resolution of TDE.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The 'SJAA Ephemeris' is identified as the monthly newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association, published 12 times annually from January through December. The statement provides the association's contact details and is explicitly dated for the May 1996 edition.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS, April 9, 1996
articles.summary: This April 9, 1996 article by Don Machholz provides an update on Comet Hyakutake's recent bright performance and its upcoming visibility as a Southern Hemisphere object, potentially including a visible tail in morning twilight for Northern Hemisphere observers. It also announces a rare lunar occultation of Comet Hale-Bopp on May 8, and briefly mentions Comet Chiron reaching perihelion and the recent discovery of Comet E1 (NEAT).

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES
articles.summary: This document presents ephemerides for several celestial objects, including comets C/1995 Y1 (Hyakutake), C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp), C/1996 B2 (Hyakutake), C/1996 B1 (Szczepanski), and 22P/Kopff, as well as minor planet 95P/Chiron. For each object, daily data is listed from late April to early June, detailing their Right Ascension, Declination, Elongation, and estimated Sky Magnitude, useful for astronomical observation planning.

articles.title: Orbital Elements
articles.summary: This document presents a table detailing the orbital elements for several celestial objects, including comets such as Hyakutake and Hale-Bopp, and the minor planet Chiron. Key data points provided for each object include perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, and orbital period. The information is sourced from various Minor Planet Circulars (MPC) and Minor Planet Electronic Circulars (MPEC).

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Status
articles.summary: This document provides an update on a telescope loaner program, listing various telescopes along with their current borrower, due date, or availability status. It notes several telescopes are available, including some in storage, and highlights a recently overhauled 13.1" Dobsonian that is now in good condition and ready for use.

articles.title: Astro Ads
articles.summary: This document features a classified advertisement for a Meade 12.5" Starfinder Dobsonian telescope, priced at $500 or open to trade. It also outlines the free submission policy for non-commercial astronomy-related ads and encourages members to submit articles for publication in the SJAA Ephemeris newsletter, providing submission details and deadlines.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document provides a directory of the current officers and board of directors for an organization, listing their positions, names, and phone numbers. It also includes contact information for Ephemeris contributors and the organization's editor.

articles.title: Lunar Phase
articles.summary: This document provides a schedule of lunar phases for a specific period. It lists the exact time (PDT) and date for the Full Moon, Last Quarter, New Moon, and First Quarter, alongside their corresponding rise, transit, and set times.

articles.title: Mercury
articles.summary: This document provides an ephemeris for the planet Mercury, detailing its distance in AU and apparent magnitude. It lists rise, transit, and set times, along with Right Ascension and Declination, for three specific dates (7th, 17th, 27th), offering essential data for observers.

articles.title: Venus
articles.summary: This document provides ephemeris data for the planet Venus, detailing its distance from Earth and apparent magnitude. It includes tabular information for three specific dates, listing rise, transit, and set times, along with its Right Ascension and Declination, which are useful for locating the planet.

articles.title: Mars
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical ephemeris data for Mars for three dates in a given month. It lists the planet's distance, magnitude, rise, transit, and set times, along with its Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec).

articles.title: Jupiter
articles.summary: This document provides an ephemeris for Jupiter, detailing its distance, apparent magnitude, and celestial coordinates (RA, Dec) for three specific dates (07, 17, 27). It also includes the rise, transit, and set times for the planet on these dates, serving as a guide for observers.

articles.title: Saturn
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical ephemeris data for the planet Saturn for three specific dates within a month (7th, 17th, 27th). It details Saturn's distance, apparent magnitude, and key observational times (rise, transit, set), along with its celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination) to assist in its observation.

articles.title: SOL Star Type G2V Intelligent Life in System ?
articles.summary: This document poses a question regarding the existence of intelligent life within a G2V star system, specifically our Sun. It then presents a table of astronomical ephemeris data, detailing rise, transit, and set times along with Right Ascension and Declination for an object observed over three different dates.

articles.title: Astronomical Twilight
articles.summary: This document presents a concise table detailing the beginning and end times for astronomical twilight across several specific Julian Dates. It provides data for three distinct dates, indicating the duration of astronomical twilight without further explanation of the phenomenon itself.

articles.title: Sidreal Time
articles.summary: The document, titled 'Sidereal Time', presents a concise table detailing the sidereal time for specific astronomical events—Transit Right, Ascension, and Local Midnight—on different dates (07, 17, 27). Each entry shows the calculated sidereal time corresponding to 00:00 on the given date. It serves as a reference for understanding sidereal time values associated with these particular celestial occurrences.

articles.title: Darkest Saturday Night: May 18
articles.summary: This document highlights "Darkest Saturday Night" on May 18, providing key astronomical times for that date. It details sunset, twilight end, moon rise, and dawn beginning, indicating optimal conditions for night sky observation.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing fees for new or renewal memberships ($15 for standard, $6 for junior) and an optional add-on for a Sky and Telescope subscription ($24). It provides instructions for submitting the form and payment, along with the treasurer's mailing address and contact information. The form also includes the organization's address, non-profit status, and indicates it is part of the May 1996 'EPHEMERIS' publication.
